identity.title: Towards Long-Horizon Interpretability: Efficient and Faithful Multi-Token Attribution for Reasoning LLMs

problem.claim: Efficiently and faithfully attribute importance for multi-token outputs in long-context, reasoning-based LLMs.

gap.claim: Existing attribution schemes reportedly require O(M·N) operations for an M-token target in an N-token context and can lose faithfulness when intermediate reasoning tokens absorb attribution mass.

contributions.claim: FlashTrace uses span-wise aggregation to compute multi-token attribution in a single pass.
A recursive attribution mechanism traces importance through intermediate reasoning chains back to source inputs.
The paper analyzes how recursive attribution affects faithfulness across reasoning chains.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish FlashTrace by combining single-pass span-wise multi-token attribution with recursive tracing through intermediate reasoning chains.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report over 130× speedup versus existing baselines on RULER, MATH, and MorehopQA tasks, while maintaining superior faithfulness.
Authors report that even one recursive hop improves faithfulness by tracing importance through the reasoning chain.

narrative_sequence.summary: Token attribution is presented as a way to identify causally important input tokens for model outputs.
Extended reasoning chains create efficiency costs and prevent attribution from propagating reliably to original inputs.
FlashTrace applies single-pass span-wise aggregation and recursive attribution through intermediate reasoning.
Experiments on long-context retrieval and multi-step reasoning tasks report substantial speedup and stronger faithfulness, with gains from one recursive hop.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a computational bottleneck with a faithfulness failure, then maps them to span-wise aggregation and recursive tracing, respectively.

lessons.interpretation: Separating failure modes can make a method’s design rationale and evidence alignment more explicit.
lessons.application: For a multi-component attribution method, state each diagnosed limitation separately and identify the mechanism intended to address it before presenting aggregate results.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when components cannot be linked to distinct failure modes or are evaluated only jointly.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the faithfulness metric, baseline identities, hardware or implementation conditions, or exact speedup measurement.
The reported meaning of “superior faithfulness” and the quantitative effect of a single recursive hop are not detailed.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported results or priority over prior methods.
